findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice machine in back storage area to be soiled with black residue on the exterior baffles. PIC was informed that the ice machine will need to be cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on July 7th (accomodating for the holiday and weekend) to ensure the machine has been properly cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed tomatoes and lettuce in the kitchen drawer cooler measure 51F with the probe. PIC was informed, and since the items were recently moved to the drawer cooler to the walk-in, the items were returned to the walk-in cooler. This violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The drawer cooler in the kitchen measured 53F with the infrared and probe thermometers. The digital display on the exterior of the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed that the cooler was not functioning and the food items inside were moved to the walk-in cooler. This cooler is not adequate for holding time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods until it is repaired. The walk-in cooler will be used until repairs are complete. A follow-up is scheduled for July 7th (accommodating the holiday and weekend) to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand sink in kitchen to be obstructed with paper towels and dish soap in sink basin. Informed PIC of issue, and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is easily accessible at all times to promote frequent and proper hand washing. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed molded sliced tomato in prep cooler drawer. PIC was informed of unsafe food, and the tomatoes were discarded. To avoid serving unsafe food to the public, ensure cut produce is clearly date marked and discarded after 7 days. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer spray bottle in the kitchen to “bleach out” test strip, indicating that the solution was too potent. PIC was informed that sanitizer was too strong, and the bottle was diluted. Ensure bleach sanitizer solutions are at an appropriate concentration to avoid toxicity. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled. The drainage line and catch tube for the soda nozzles were also soiled and had mold growth. One of the catch tubes were clogged as well. PIC was informed of the issue and plans to use a designated brush to clean the catch tubes. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/20/2025 to ensure the soda nozzles and catch tubes have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed produce in prep cooler (tomato, lettuce, onion) and walk-in cooler (salads, creamer, milk) to have no date mark. Informed PIC that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods that are considered ready-to-eat need to be date marked and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up has been scheduled for 3/20/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed hood in kitchen to be soiled dust and grease. Observed chest freezer in back storage area to be soiled with old food (french fries). Informed PIC that chest freezer and hood are in need of a cleaning. Routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces prevents cross-contamination with food and food-contact surfaces. Ensure that surfaces are clean for next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed floor of walk-in cooler to be soiled with food debris. Informed PIC that floor needed a cleaning. Keeping flooring in the facility clean not only prevents cross-contamination, but can prevent pest infestation as well. Ensure flooring is clean by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 3-304.12: Observed blade of knife used for food prep to be stored under pizza oven on counter top. Knife was moved during inspection. FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

(B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.comment:

Hand sinks in both restrooms are missing hand washing signs. One is completely absent the other in ripped mostly off of the hand towel dispenser. Hand wash signs were provided to the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 
Observed containers of seasoning to be stored on bread crates that are not at least six inches above the floor. Crates are also difficult to clean around and often lead to other issues. Discontinue this practice and provide proper storage for these items.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed 3 soda guns at the bar to be soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated debris. The soda guns were properly cleaned during inspection. Washed, rinsed and sanitized. 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed a box of fries on the floor of the walk in cooler. A bag of raw uncut onions are also observed on the floor in the back storage area. Put food up when it arrives from the truck. Truck was yesterday. 3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloth to be stored on the coffin cooler during lunch rush. Cloth was placed back into sanitizer container. 3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed boxes of single-use articles to be stored on the floor in the facility. 4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Soda nozzles in the bar area were observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residue. Ensure these surfaces are soaked and sanitized to prevent the potential contamination of the contact surfaces with the food items being served. Ensure this process is conducted at a frequency that prevents this accumulation.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Overall the facility is in need of a deep clean, especially in hard to reach areas, under equipment, and along the areas where the walls meet the floor int he bar area and back storage area. Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris and soil residue. This cleaning will also discourage potential pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: Facility did not have employee health reporting agreements on file. A copy was left with the facility and the PIC was making copies during the inspection. These forms shall be available during the next routine inspection and kept on file for display upon inspector request. The employees were signing them today during the inspection.
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed that the racks of pizza ovens are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). Maintain properly clean and ready to use. Pizza oven racks were properly cleaned at time of inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430. Employees shall obtain the handler certification within 30 days of hire.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Ice bin at the TIKI bar is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). The ice bin was cleaned and sanitized immediately.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Observed sleeves of single use cups to be stored on the floor next tot he garbage can at the front bar. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C). Cups were moved up off of the floor immediately.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07  Not all of the certified food managers have completed the required online food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Observed raw beef stored next to lettuce and deli meats in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods separated from raw so they are protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Chili is 125°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F. The chili had been hot holding for approximately 2 hours. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Observed deli meat packages to be thawing at room temperature on the prep table in the kitchen. Time and temperature control for safety (TICS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13. Properly thaw foods for safety. Foods were placed into the cooler for thawing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

Also, some small black ants are observed on the floor in the dry stoarge. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate all pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

Reference 4-301.12(A)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil residue present on counters and shelves in the upstairs kitchen. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12 (A&B) Observed floors in the dry stoarge in back, the dry storage upstairs and ktichen upstairs to be heavily soiled. The soil is even greater in hard to reach areas. Clean and maintain clean. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) Observed a ceiling tile to be missing from the restroom downstairs. Replace ceiling tile. Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.  Reference 6-501.11.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: Managers are not allerge trained. Provide allergen training befor next routine inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Boxes with raw, thawing fish were observed on top of a keg in the walkin cooler. Boxes of fish were moved and placed on an inverted crate in the walkin. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store raw foods below/separate from ready to eat foods, and do not store raw foods on top of kegs or cases of beverages.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 280 - A) Slaw in walkin cooler had small plastic portion cup inside. Plastic portion cup was discarded. B) Red plastic cup was observed in bulk popping corn storage tub. Plastic cup was removed from storage tub. Ready to eat foods shall be handled and dispensed in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. Suitable utensils (spoons, scoops, gloves, deli tissue, etc.) must be used for dispensing all foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Duct tape was observed along the seam of the lower, back right corner to the table holding the grill. Remove the duct tape and provide a proper repair. B) Black trim on ice machine below scoop holder was cracked. Seal the area of damaged trim on the ice machine. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) pizza trays; B) cup holding meat thermometer (debris in bottom); C) Coors Light bucket used for storage of utensils (dust/debris in bottom); D) hood filters over cooking equipment (grease/dust); E) top edge around breading pan (gross buildup); F) meat thermometer. Properly wash, rinse, and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) grill - waste tray/area between tray and grill surface (carbon/debris); B) (R) table holding grill (dust/debris - area below grill and lower storage shelf); C) (R) counter under microwave and food warmer (crumbs/debris); D) (R) top of microwave below pizza ovens (dust/crumbs); E) (R) fryer - inside (dust/debris) & bottom underneath/sides/legs (grease); F) inside oven; G) area between range top and waste tray of stove (dust/grease); & H) outside surfaces of pickle bucket (grease). Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - A) Clean utensils were stored in soiled Coors Light bucket (see #22), and whisks were observed with food surfaces facing up out of the container. Food debris was stuck on some of the utensils. B) Meat thermometer was stored in soiled cup (see #22). Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Store all utensils with handles extended up from storage containers, and maintain storage areas clean. Keep soiled utensils separate from clean utensils.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - Rolls of plastic wrap on lower shelf of table holding grill were in direct contact with soiled shelf. Also, boxes holding other single service items, such as storage bags, had grease splash on them, and crumbs/pieces of carbon had fallen in a few of the boxes. Storage of single service articles was discussed with owner. All single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Store items in plastic, cleanable storage containers below the grill if single service articles are not adequately protected in original containers or move items to another area of storage purposes. Store plastic wrap on a clean surface.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1110 & 1120 - A) Basin of porcelain handsink in women's room had cracks in it. Seal the cracks in the handsink. B) Cloth towel dispenser in men's room was jammed and brown smudge was present on exposed portion of towel. Cloth towel was removed and roll of paper towels were placed in men's room. C) Faucet handles and top around kitchen handsink were soiled with dust/buildup. Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Small flies were observed in the restrooms (2 to 3 total) and at the bar on the soda lines/in the floor to wall juncture below the bar (+12). Manager noted the breeding area was found within the crevice at the floor to wall juncture behind the ice bin/soda lines. Heavy buildup of debris was present, and fairly significant gaps were noted throughout the bar floor to wall junctures. Thoroughly along floor to wall junctures and seal all areas where gaps, cracks, and crevices are present at the bar along the junctures of floors/walls and in floor tiles. Effective measures to minimize the presence pests shall be utilized. If cleaning and general repairs do not alleviate the issue then contact pest control operator for additional service.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Floor in kitchen was soiled along the walls/in corners, especially behind oven and in the corner behind the cooler. Clean the floor in the kitchen. B) (R) Floor to wall juncture throughout bar had accumulation of debris. Gaps are present along junctures, and tiles under 3 part sink had gaps. Clean the floor to wall juncture and provide proper repairs throughout the entire bar (see #35a & general comments). C) Piece of coving was missing behind door in men's room, and gaps were present at top of coving in corners of women's room. Provide proper repairs in restrooms along coving and floor to wall juncture. Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) The following issues were observed in the Women's room - 1) gap around plumbing below handsink, 2) small holes below toilet paper dispenser, & 3) chunks of grout missing along corner of the wall next to toilet. B) The following issues were observed in the men's room - 1) duct tape over the light switch & 2) section of tile/grout missing at lower corner behind the door. Provide proper repairs in the restrooms. Walls must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Conditions at floor to wall juncture of bar has allowed for the proliferation of small flies (see #35a & #36 for details) The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents. Thoroughly clean and seal the floor to wall juncture throughout the bar. Clean and repair area where small flies are breeding by 5/29/13 (see general comments for details).
